To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the series-elastic component of human triceps-surae muscle stores elastic energy during the eccentric phase of walking and running.

(1) in walking and running, the series elastic component of the triceps surae is stretched during the eccentric phase, and recoils during the concentric phase; (2) the contractile component of the tricep surae muscle is active during both the eccentric and concentric phase of the step cycle; (3) the contractile velocity of the contractile component is low during the eccentric and concentic phase of the stepcycle.
the series-elastic component is the main contributor to the length changes of the muscle–tendon complex during natural activities like walking or running.

the question how the muscle-tendon system of the calf is used during locomotion, and how it contributes to the mechanical work of locomotion.

the muscle-tendon unit of the triceps surae in humans behaves as an efficient elastic spring during the eccentric phase of walking or running.
the MTC of the calf muscle behaves as an elastic spring during the eccentric phase of the gait cycle.
the muscle-tendon system is a highly effective spring-mass system that stores energy in walking, running or squat jumping.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muscle-tendon system behaves as a spring-mass system in walking, running, and squat jumping.

the muscle-tendon unit is used in such a way that the elastic component of the MTC is loaded in the eccentric phase of walking and running and unloaded in the concentric phases, and that in the eccentric phases the CC is used at lengths well beyond the optimum for force production.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the muscle-tendon apparatus of the human calf is designed to store energy in the SEC, which can be released at a higher velocity, and that this mechanism allows the CC to operate at a lower, more efficient, velocity.
the SEC plays an important role in the mechanical behaviour of the human MTC.
the muscle-tendon system of the triceps surae is well designed for efficient locomotion and for the storage and release of energy during locomotor activities.
